sources.title: Constraining Conformal Field Theories with A Higher Spin Symmetry

evidence.text: Extract twist-one light-cone OPE contributions and construct quasi-bilocals B and F−. Establish normalized actions [Qs,B/F−]=(∂1^(s−1)+∂2^(s−1))B/F− for even s. Infinitely many resulting differential constraints, conformal covariance and cluster decomposition fix free-field pairings.

sources.title: Comments on Chern-Simons Contact Terms in Three Dimensions

evidence.text: Compute contact terms through perturbative RG flows and background-field diagrams; use localization results to extract κff=−(1/2π)∂²m Im FS3 and κfr=(1/2π)∂m Re FS3 at m=0 on the unit sphere. Compare relative counterterms across proposed dual descriptions.

sources.title: Constraining conformal field theories with a higher spin symmetry in $d > 3$ dimensions

evidence.text: Quasi-bilocals B, F− and V−− are constructed from stress-tensor OPEs. Their charge action is reduced to endpoint derivatives. Higher-spin Ward identities, conformal properties, permutation symmetry and cluster decomposition fix their correlators; OPE expansions then reconstruct current correlators.

evidence.text: Use derivative functionals at the modular self-dual point β=1. Laguerre values and derivatives are evaluated by three-term recurrences.

evidence.text: Expand observables in Virasoro conformal blocks, average OPE products using Wick contractions, and evaluate heavy-state integrals semiclassically. The Cardy density and DOZZ-related universal OPE function serve as modular and fusion crossing kernels.

sources.title: CFT Correlators and Mapping Class Group Averages

evidence.text: The natural nondegenerate pairing identifies V^C(Σ̂) with End(V^C(Σ)). Diagonal mapping class action becomes conjugation; Schur’s lemma makes the invariant subspace one-dimensional under irreducibility. Invariance of the pairing then establishes nonvanishing of an average with d_Σ(x) ≠ 0.

sources.title: 3d gravity as a random ensemble

evidence.text: Poisson rewriting of integer-spin sums supplies T transforms; expansion of the S-constraint is argued to produce an SL(2,Z) symmetrizer as ℏ→0. Appendix C distinguishes the normalized internal projector from external spin sums, whose combination is claimed to give modular images with weight one.

evidence.text: Empty-torus and empty-annulus blocks require different treatment because they are not normalizable in the Verlinde inner product. Vandermonde kernels define spectral matrix potentials; their functional inverses determine density two-point functions.
